utility.value: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
utility.notes: Directly checked on 2026-10-12: LADWP states that it supplies electricity to residents and businesses in the City of Los Angeles. This does not establish service to every address in Los Angeles County.

value.name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
value.notes: LADWP is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like Pasadena Water and Power) — it generates and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving the City of Los Angeles in the sources reviewed this session.

permit_authority.value: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
permit_authority.notes: Directly checked on 2026-10-12: LADBS handles City of Los Angeles permits. LADWP separately handles utility interconnection; city permit approval is not permission to operate on the grid.

permit_url.notes: Same LADBS direct-fetch limitation as permit_authority.

interconnection_url.notes: LADWP publishes a separate interconnection application and approval process. Type 1 ends with a LADWP NEM Permission to Operate notice after the applicable city and utility approvals, commissioning and meter work; no total duration is asserted.

value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

value.name: LADBS online photovoltaic Express Permit application (contractors only)
value.required_when: Only rooftop PV on a one- or two-family dwelling meeting every condition in P/GI 2026-003, page 4 section 15; systems outside that scope need their applicable permit route.

value.name: Approved photovoltaic plans generated by the LADBS online system
value.required_when: For the eligible Express installation; install to these plans and keep the permit and applicable approved plans available for LADBS inspection.

value.name: Separate LADWP online interconnection application with the documentation and photos required for the applicable system type
value.required_when: For grid interconnection. LADWP sends the Interconnection/NEM Work Request number after the application; the number is not a prerequisite document for submitting that application.

value.name: LADWP single-line diagram and interconnection agreement
value.required_when: LADWP lists these for PV-only systems over 10 kW and up to 30 kW, single phase. In that table, plot/site plan and load schedule requirements apply to new construction/ADU projects only. Other sizes and PV-plus-storage systems have separate requirements.

required_documents.notes: City permit documents and utility interconnection documents are separate and conditional. This is not a universal engineering checklist for all residential PV systems. A separate building permit may be required for structural support. Sources checked 2026-10-12; the Express bulletin was revised 2026-06-10.

value: Obtain the applicable LADBS permit before beginning work, and request inspection before covering or concealing the work.

When ready, request LADBS inspection online or through 311. Keep the work visible and have a permit copy and approved plans where plan review was required; the Building Card applies to Building Permits only.

Complete the applicable inspections and obtain LADBS final inspection approval. Systems qualifying under LAMC 91.106.5.1 generally require no more than one city inspection; a failed inspection may require another, and LADWP can inspect separately.

For a qualifying LADWP Type 1 interconnection, complete the applicable utility final approvals, commissioning and meter work, and obtain LADWP NEM Permission to Operate. LADBS approval alone is not permission to operate on the grid.
inspection_steps.notes: City and utility steps are distinct; their inclusion here does not establish one universal sequence for every project. Obtain the applicable LADWP Type 1 pre-construction approval before construction. Type 1 is limited to eligible aggregate systems up to 30 kW without a service-panel upgrade, three-phase service, non-NEM cogeneration or multi-meter arrangements. No inspection appointment or total interconnection time is promised.

timeline_days.notes: Not yet verified: no numeric residential permit-review duration was established. The eligible LADBS Express pathway has no plan check, but that is not a same-day promise or a duration through LADWP Permission to Operate. See LA_EXPRESS_2026_003 and LADWP_TYPES_20261012 for the separate processes.

value.program_or_pathway: LADBS residential rooftop PV Express Permit; LAMC 91.106.5.1 streamlined eligibility
other_conditions: LAMC 91.106.5.1 explicitly sets a 10 kW AC nameplate ceiling for the streamlined PV pathway, with applicable fire, structural, electrical, safety and building-height requirements; this is not a citywide maximum system size.
The PV Express route in P/GI 2026-003 section 15 is online for contractors only, for a rooftop system on a one- or two-family dwelling that meets all listed conditions.
The Express PV AC system must be 120/240 V single phase and the service panel must not exceed 225 A; no GFCI or AFCI overcurrent devices are installed in the inverter AC output.

Section 15 limits central/string systems to two inverters, up to four strings and one combiner box per inverter; microinverter systems have up to four branch circuits, with the specified DC arc-fault protection.
Hybrid systems, building-integrated PV and photovoltaic roll roofing do not qualify under this Express PV checklist; structural support may need a separate building permit.
PV with energy storage must meet the separate section 16 requirements, including the applicable Fire Department plan check and permit; PV-only eligibility is not automatic battery approval.
LADWP interconnection eligibility is separate. Type 1 can cover qualifying systems up to 30 kW aggregate, subject to its service-panel, phase, cogeneration and meter exclusions.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Checked 2026-10-12. The 10 kW AC unit is supported by the municipal streamlined-permit rule, not inferred by convention. The June 10, 2026 Express bulletin states a 10 kW total PV capacity limit and supplies additional pathway conditions. Do not merge these with the utility Type 1 size threshold.

value.name: City of Los Angeles electrical permit issuing fee
value.notes: Per LAMC as published by American Legal Publishing, checked 2026-10-24. Amount dates from a 2011 amendment; LADBS fee pages were not accessible.

value.name: City of Los Angeles minimum electrical inspection fee
value.unit: per electrical installation, paid when equipment fees total less (LAMC 93.0220, 98.0412(a))
value.notes: LAMC 98.0412 says the minimum includes the issuing fee; LAMC 93.0220 says it is in addition to the issuing fee. Not resolved.

value.name: City of Los Angeles solar voltaic equipment fees
value.unit: $6 per module; $6 per combiner box; inverter by rating: up to 3 kW $8, over 3 to 5 kW $18, over 5 to 20 kW $27, over 20 to 50 kW $39, over 50 to 100 kW $71.50, over 100 kW $111 (LAMC 93.0218)
value.notes: Code text, not a LADBS fee calculator result. Final fee is set when the application is submitted.

permit_fees.notes: Components from the Los Angeles Municipal Code (amlegal), checked 2026-10-24. LADBS pages and fee calculator were blocked, so current LADBS charges, any Express-permit flat fee, and any separate structural building permit fee are not verified. LADWP interconnection charges are separate and not recorded as city fees.

rebates.notes: LADWP's 'Solar Rooftops Program' referenced in some sources appears to be a separate leased/shared-solar program (mentioning lease payments to participants), distinct from a standard rebate for a customer-owned system — not recorded here as a rebate since its structure was not independently confirmed as a rebate in this session.

official_contacts.notes: Contact details found via consistent search-engine indexing; not independently fetched this session (both domains 403 blocked).
